function: Excluded as above_phy: the learned policy decides random-access back-off, pilot selection and transmit power per packet under deadlines (p. 7, "distributed access policy"); channel estimation and combining are classical (pp. 3-4).
notes: Reason above_phy. The learned element is a distributed random-access policy: p. 1: "allows the users to dynamically and independently choose their pilots and transmit powers", under packet deadlines and fairness; p. 7 (Remark 2): "learn a distributed access policy". The physical layer is not learned: MMSE channel estimation (p. 3) and MR/ZF receive combining (p. 4, p. 11) are fixed, and the unsupervised GRU policy network (pp. 8-9) maximizes an expected sum-priority built from a closed-form rate proxy. If a reviewer reads the learned power control as a physical-layer decision, the work would still fail the function check: pilot selection and power control for random access are not among the seven areas. The system check does not apply (BS with M = 100 receive antennas, p. 10). Baselines are non-learned access schemes plus VDN and QMIX on a collision-only model (pp. 10-13).
